description: FSF sample data for `make demo`. All text is fictional and only illustrates the tool.

steps.title: Intuition: flow speed saturates
steps.body: Old notebook page. Hunch: under rising forcing, the flow speed does not grow without bound but levels off.
steps.author_statement: Written in a paper notebook last autumn; typed in today.

steps.title: Reading notes: three earlier models
steps.body:
# Reading notes

- Model A: linear response, no saturation.
- Model B: logistic saturation, fixed exponent.
- Model C: empirical fit, no mechanism.

None explains a variable exponent.

steps.title: Hypothesis H1: saturation follows a power law
steps.body: H1: v(t) approaches 1 with (1 - v)^alpha, alpha = 1.5.

steps.title: Formula v1
steps.body:
dv/dt = k (1 - v)^alpha

with k = 0.8 and alpha = 1.5 (from H1).

steps.title: Solver prototype
steps.author_statement: Archive attached so the code itself is preserved, not just the commit reference.

steps.title: Numerical experiment 1
steps.body:
# Run 1

Solver prototype, k = 0.8, alpha = 1.5, 80 steps.

Result: converges, but the fitted exponent is closer to 1.3 than 1.5.

steps.title: Hypothesis H1′: the exponent depends on forcing
steps.body: H1′: alpha is not fixed; it decreases with forcing.
steps.author_statement: Experiment 1 contradicted the fixed exponent, so the hypothesis changed.

steps.title: Numerical experiment 2
steps.body:
# Run 2

Formula v2, three forcing levels. Residual drops from 0.041 to 0.012.

steps.title: Side idea: lattice model
steps.body: Tried a lattice discretisation as an alternative. Setup later turned out to be wrong.

steps.title: Figure 2: exponent versus forcing
steps.body: Plot of fitted alpha against forcing F for run 2.

steps.title: Preprint: forcing-dependent saturation
steps.author_statement: Archived preprint; the DOI is the strongest third-party reference.

steps.statement: Only noticed later: Figure 2 also re-plots the run 1 data as a baseline.

steps.text: Clarification: k = 0.8 was taken from Model B in the reading notes.
